title: 夜市經濟學
titleEn: The economics of the night market
summary: Rents, viral posts and regulation behind the noise.
paragraphs: 夜市向來被視為臺灣庶民文化的縮影，然而在熱鬧喧囂的背後，其實蘊藏著一套獨特的經濟邏輯。
攤商多半以家庭為單位經營，憑藉低廉的租金與彈性的營業時間，在激烈的競爭中求生存。
近年來，隨著食材成本與攤位租金節節攀升，部分攤販不得不調漲售價，引發「夜市不再便宜」的感嘆。
與此同時，網路評論與社群媒體的影響力與日俱增，一則爆紅的貼文便可能讓默默無名的小攤一夕之間大排長龍。
另一方面，政府為了改善環境衛生與公共安全，持續推動攤位登記與夜市轉型，卻也不免與攤商的生計產生摩擦。
夜市的未來，取決於能否在傳統風味與現代管理之間找到平衡點。
translation: Night markets have long been seen as a microcosm of Taiwan's popular culture, but behind the bustle lies a distinctive economic logic.
Most stalls are family-run, surviving fierce competition thanks to low rents and flexible hours.
In recent years, as ingredient costs and stall rents keep climbing, some vendors have had to raise prices, prompting sighs that "night markets aren't cheap anymore".
Meanwhile, the influence of online reviews and social media grows by the day: one viral post can give an unknown stall a long queue overnight.
On the other hand, the government keeps pushing stall registration and night-market transformation to improve hygiene and public safety, which inevitably creates friction with vendors' livelihoods.
The future of the night market depends on finding a balance between traditional flavor and modern management.
